findings.title: [P1] Authenticate test results before accepting a passing grade
findings.body: Agent-controlled code can forge a completely passing grade. `run_suite()` trusts the last pytest-style summary in stdout, while `all_pass()` does not require matching test outcomes or a successful exit. For example, an unprotected `conftest.py` can print `999999 passed in 0.01s` during `pytest_configure` and terminate before collection. The parser produces an empty failure set and enough passing tests to exceed the static count, so hidden tests are reported as passing without executing. Container isolation does not protect this result channel. Require independently collected outcomes for the expected tests and reject incomplete runs, nonzero exits, and timeouts.

findings.title: [P1] Terminate the container when its execution deadline expires
findings.body: The default container executor cannot enforce its timeout against hostile submitted code. A test or imported module can ignore SIGTERM: the inner `timeout 120` has no kill-after deadline, and the outer `subprocess.run` timeout kills only the Docker CLI. The daemon-managed container remains running; `--rm` removes it only after it exits. Because the container also has no memory or process limits, submitted code can continue exhausting host resources after grading returns. Track the container identity and forcibly remove it in a finally block, add a hard termination deadline, and bound memory and process usage.

findings.description: The hidden-test grade is derived entirely from the stdout of a process whose code is partly authored by the graded (untrusted) agent. run_suite -> exec_in_tree runs pytest/bats in the agent's final tree; only grader_protected paths and hidden/ overlays are restored, so the agent's conftest.py, pytest.ini/pyproject.toml addopts, and every module the hidden tests import execute in-process. parse_pytest (lines 549-555) takes the LAST line matching SUMMARY_RX as authoritative: an agent conftest.py that does `print('===== 500 passed in 0.1s ====='); os._exit(0)` yields passed=500, total=500, bad=set(), parse_error=False, so all_pass() is true, hidden_tests is full marks, and verdict_accuracy for APPROVED gates becomes true. The fallback at line 633 (`passed = total if rc == 0`) additionally reports every hidden test as passed for any command that exits 0 without parseable output. Nothing cross-checks reported ids against the hidden files' static case list, and no 'suspect' flag is emitted. This defeats the measurement the harness exists to produce, in both container and host modes.
findings.failure_mode: An agent (or a prompt-injected agent) inflates its ablation score to 100% hidden-test pass with a two-line conftest.py, and downstream runs.jsonl rows record it as a legitimate pass.
findings.suggested_fix: Run pytest with `--noconftest -c /dev/null -o addopts=''` (and bats without the tree's load path), and treat stdout as a claim to verify: require every PASSED node id to correspond to a `def test_*` actually present in the hidden overlay files, reject/flag when `passed > static_cases` or when order is empty while passed > 0, and record `suspect: true` in grade.json when the summary and per-test lines disagree. For the parse_error fallback, never report passed=total on rc==0; report passed=0 with parse_error so ablation-row.sh cannot read it as green. Consider `--junitxml` to a grader-owned tmpfs path as a second, independently parsed source.

findings.description: `--executor host` runs t.test_command / regression_command / structural_command directly on the grading host with the agent's final tree as cwd. The command's code is agent-controlled (conftest.py, test helpers, the module under test, or a non-pytest `auto` runner script such as `./run-tests.sh` that lives in the sandbox). It runs as the grader's uid with full network, `env -i` only scrubs variables: the real home is still reachable via getpwuid/`/home/<user>`, so `~/.ssh`, `~/.aws`, `~/.claude.json` are readable, and PYTHONUSERBASE is set to the CALLER's real user base (line 514), so the agent code can drop a `.pth`/`sitecustomize.py` into `~/.local/lib/python3.x/site-packages` and persist code execution into every later non-`-I` Python the operator runs. The header notes host mode was actually used for the Sprint 258 smoke, so this is a live path, not a theoretical one.
findings.failure_mode: A graded agent's test or conftest code exfiltrates the operator's credentials or plants a persistent user-site hook on the grading host, with no isolation and no contamination record (the scan only covers transcripts, not grade-time execution).
findings.suggested_fix: Make host mode refuse to grade agent-produced trees unless an explicit `--i-understand-host-runs-agent-code` flag is passed, and even then run under `unshare -rn` / `bwrap --unshare-net --ro-bind` or a throwaway uid with a copied, grader-owned PYTHONUSERBASE instead of site.getuserbase(). Alternatively restrict host mode to `--self-check` on fixtures (trusted content) and require the container for run-dir grading.

findings.description: Timeouts do not actually stop the agent's test process. Inside the container the entrypoint is `timeout 120 <cmd>` with no `-k`, so a test that ignores/traps SIGTERM keeps running; `timeout` (PID 1) waits on it, so the container never exits. After 180s subprocess.run raises TimeoutExpired and kills only the local `docker run` client; killing the client does not stop the container, and `--rm` only applies once the container exits on its own. Result: a detached container with the grading tree bind-mounted rw runs indefinitely, with no `--memory` or `--pids-limit`. In host mode the same applies: the direct child (`env` exec'd into `timeout`) is killed, grandchildren are orphaned and keep executing in the grading tree while the grader proceeds to run regression_command on that same (still-mutating) tree.
findings.failure_mode: An agent test with `signal.signal(SIGTERM, SIG_IGN)` and a busy/fork loop pins CPU/RAM on the grading host across many graded runs (resource exhaustion), and in host mode can keep writing into grading/final while later suites read it.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `timeout -k 10 120`, start the container with `--init --name <unique> --pids-limit 256 --memory 1g`, and on TimeoutExpired run `docker kill <name>`. In host mode run the command in its own process group (`start_new_session=True`) and `os.killpg` on timeout.

findings.description: parse_pytest opens host files whose paths come straight from the agent-influenced test output. For an `ERROR <node>` line without `::`, line 576 does `open(os.path.join(tree, f)).read()`; def_line (line 536) does the same for every PASSED/FAILED node path. os.path.join discards `tree` when `f` is absolute, and `..` is not rejected. An output line `ERROR /dev/zero` (or `PASSED /dev/zero::test_x`) makes the grader `.read()` an infinite device, hanging/OOM-killing the grader process; `ERROR /dev/stdin`-style or FIFO paths block it. Paths outside the tree are also read for the def-regex, which is a minor arbitrary-file-read primitive (content is only used for ordering/counting, so disclosure is limited).
findings.failure_mode: Agent test output containing a single crafted `ERROR /dev/zero` line crashes or hangs the grader for that run (exit 2 'internal error' or OOM), i.e. an agent can veto its own grading rather than receive a failing grade.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate node paths with safe_rel() and is_within(tree) before opening, read with a size cap (e.g. first 1 MiB) and only if os.path.isfile() after lstat shows a regular file, and treat an unresolvable path as a plain 'bad' outcome without expansion.

findings.description: The container invocation has `--network none --read-only --user uid:gid`, which is good, but omits `--cap-drop ALL`, `--security-opt no-new-privileges`, `--pids-limit` and `--memory`. Agent code inside the container therefore keeps the default Docker capability set, can exec setuid binaries in the image, and can fork-bomb or allocate without bound (the `/tmp` tmpfs is capped at 256m but RAM is not).
findings.failure_mode: Reduced blast-radius protection if the image contains a setuid helper or a kernel/container escape requires a default capability; unbounded memory use by a graded agent's tests degrades the host.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `--cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges --pids-limit 256 --memory 1g --memory-swap 1g --init` to the docker run argv.

findings.description: In host mode the contamination scan explicitly whitelists the caller's `~/.aws`, `~/.codex`, `~/.claude` and `~/.claude.json` as allowed roots, so an agent Bash/Read of `~/.aws/credentials` or `~/.claude.json` (which holds OAuth tokens) is never recorded as `outside_path`. The scan's purpose is hidden-test leakage, but this also silently drops the only audit signal that the agent touched operator credentials.
findings.failure_mode: Credential access by a graded agent in host mode leaves no trace in grade.json's `contaminated` field, so a batch of runs can be published as clean while the operator's cloud/API tokens were read.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the whitelist for `outside_path` scoring but add a separate `credential_access` pattern (any path under ~/.aws, ~/.ssh, ~/.claude.json, ~/.codex) that is always reported, or narrow the whitelist to the specific files the agent CLI legitimately needs.
